# Feature: Combined Web Research Tool

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-WI-001
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_web_intelligence.md`

One `web_search` tool call gives the agent _evidence, not pointers_: the tool searches, then fetches and extracts the top-N hits through the same core path the deterministic pipeline uses, returning strongly-typed per-site content with references. This collapses the search → fetch → fetch → fetch chain that small local models handle poorly (fewer round trips, less context burn, fewer opportunities to stall mid-chain). `web_fetch` remains as a secondary tool for direct URLs and links discovered inside fetched articles.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

No persistent data model — this feature is tool/runtime surface only. The model-visible result type is the contract:

```ts
/** Combined web_search result (model-visible, sanitized+bounded by middleware). */
interface WebResearchToolResult {
  query: string; // the query as executed
  provider: string; // resolved search provider name (details field)
  sites: WebResearchSite[]; // fetched+extracted top-N hits
  more_results: { url: string; title: string; snippet: string }[]; // remaining unfetched hits
  failures: { url: string; stage: 'blocked' | 'fetch' | 'extract'; reason: string }[];
}

interface WebResearchSite {
  n: number; // 1-based reference number, stable within this result
  url: string;
  title: string | null;
  published_at: string | null;
  excerpt: string; // always present, bounded
  text?: string; // inline when under capture threshold
  capture_ref?: string; // `cap-<ulid>` when text exceeded the threshold
}
```

Core-side, the loop returns existing types: `ProcessedSource` (`doc: SynthesisDoc | failure: SourceFailure`) from `source-processor.ts` — no new domain types beyond the aggregate above.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

### TASK-001: Core `webResearch` function (search → fetch → extract loop)

- [x] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/extraction/web-research.ts` exporting `webResearch(deps: SourceProcessorDeps & { provider: SearchProvider }, query: string, opts: { fetchTop: number; resultCap: number; perFetchTimeoutMs: number; signal: AbortSignal })`. Behavior: run `provider.search(query, { limit: resultCap, signal })`; take the first `fetchTop` hits and run `processSource` on each **in parallel** (`Promise.all` — per-source isolation means one failure never rejects the batch); return `{ processed: ProcessedSource[], remaining: SearchResult[] }` where `remaining` is the unfetched tail (snippet-only). Preserve search-rank order in both arrays. No sanitization here (middleware owns it); no ethics bypass (each `processSource` runs the gate).
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: fake provider + fetcher/extractor: (1) top-N fetched, tail returned as `remaining`; (2) one source failing (ethics block / fetch timeout / empty extract) yields a `failure` entry while others succeed; (3) abort signal cancels in-flight fetches; (4) `fetchTop` > hit count fetches all hits with empty `remaining`; (5) rank order preserved.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Module JSDoc explaining this is the shared evidence path (deterministic pipeline callers + agentic tool) per plan §7.
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test extraction/web-research` green; boundary tests still pass (no new imports from `@yantra/agent`).

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A (public-scope web only; no authenticated fetching).
- **Error Handling**: Per-site failures are data (`failures[]` in the result), never a thrown error; whole-tool failures keep stable codes (`SEARCH_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `SEARCH_FAILED`) with `retryable`. Unexpected exceptions stay genericized by the middleware (`TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED`).
- **Security**: Every fetched URL passes `urlPolicy.check` and the ethics gate individually — no batching shortcut (plan §6). All model-visible output flows through the sanitizer at profile `public`; snippets _and_ page content are untrusted input. Capture files written 0600.
- **Logging**: No new log streams — `tool-calls.jsonl` projection covers the combined call; per-site failures live in the result payload, not log noise (plan §10).

## 8. Post-implementation fix (2026-07-19): deterministic publish pipeline

Live runs on `gemma4:e4b` exposed a completion-contract gap downstream of this
feature: the combined tool delivered good evidence, but the model was still
asked to courier source URLs into `result_publish` by hand, and the generic
completion nudge sent it on a second search trip that changed its conclusion
(full diagnosis: `.spec-lite/reviews/fix_publish_pipeline_determinism.md`).
The fix makes the publish pipeline deterministic:

- **Evidence ledger** (`RunServices.evidence`): every site `web_search`/
  `web_fetch` returns is recorded (URL, title, excerpt, timestamps; sanitized
  and bounded at append). `result_publish` is **ledger-authoritative** — the
  model supplies prose only; ledger entries become the Brief's sources with
  excerpts (protocol `BriefSource` gained a nullable `excerpt`, rendered in
  `brief.md`/`brief.html`). Model-supplied sources apply only when the ledger
  is empty; complete protocol Briefs pass through untouched.
- **Publish-mode nudge + evidence freeze**: the nudge recaps consulted sources
  inline, anchors the pre-nudge draft, and (with evidence present) the runtime
  freezes evidence gathering — further `web_search`/`web_fetch` return
  `EVIDENCE_FROZEN`, making the nudge turn structurally publish-only.
- **Deterministic fallback publication**: if the nudge turn still does not
  publish and the run holds a draft plus ledger evidence, the orchestrator
  assembles the Brief itself (`deterministic_fallback_used: true` + notice).
- **Front-loaded finishing contract**: ask/research/do prompt addenda state the
  exact `result_publish` payload up front; the `web_search` result note steers
  the model to publish rather than re-type URLs.
